summary: Mid-pilot sync focused on network-level latency spikes between Aurelia's VPCs and Redwood Private nodes. Reviewed recent latencies, discussed kernel rollback tradeoffs, KV cache warmup, and egress shaping. Agreed on short smoke tests and a longer burn-in. Next steps assigned for config handoff and test windows.
topics: latency smoothing, routing fallbacks, kernel/quant kernel upgrade, KV cache warmup, egress shaping, SOC2/audit logs, pilot timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): ok everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh we got a fairly tight agenda — latency spikes, canary routing, and the kernel rollback plan. quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya (Aurelia): Maya here, Rafael, Anika, Samir on.
[00:18] Rafael (SRE): hey all. we've been seeing two recurring spike patterns: ingress jitter around 120–180ms for ~30s bursts and then a 400ms tail when KV misses happen.
[00:30] Priya (SE): yeah that matches the traces we got last week, some of the transcribed RPCs show repeated reconnects after that tail.
[00:38] Samir (Network Eng): the path between our az-west-2 VPC peer and the redwood-private subnet goes through a transit gateway and then a partner colo; there's a bursty NAT device there, could be causing egress serialization.
[00:52] Lucas (Solutions Eng): to add, our continuous batcher stops sending to the GPU while the K V cache refill is happening, so you see the latency amplify. sometimes the pipeline stalls for an extra 2 tokens while the cache warms.
[01:10] Anika (CTO): ps, from a success criteria perspective we need 99th < 250ms for user-facing calls. if we can't hit that with the pilot, procurement will push back.
[01:22] Jordan (AE): understood. quick qual — are the user calls primarily short chat turns (50–150 tokens) or longer generation?
[01:29] Maya: mostly short turns, single-turn assistant, some multi-turn flows for internal triage but 80% are 20–70 tokens.
[01:36] Priya: ok so small sequences — that tends to amplify tail latency effects. two knobs we discussed: routing policy (prefer local AZs or fall back to compatible quant models) and KV-cache prewarm windows.
[01:50] Rafael: can you remind us the difference between the quant fallback and the routing fallback? we had some notes but lost the context.
[01:58] Priya: sure — routing fallback means we route to a different Redwood node or region with spare capacity, possibly higher cost. quant fallback is serving the same model but a quantized variant that may be slightly lower quality but costs less and is faster. both have tradeoffs for hallucination risk and quality.
[02:14] Samir: if we route cross-region we add ~60–80ms baseline, which kills the 99th target. so we want to avoid cross-region unless absolutely necessary.
[02:22] Jordan: right — so the goal is to keep routing local and instead reduce the KV-cache miss rate and smooth egress.
[02:30] Priya: we've built a small egress shaping proposal: burst tokenization window where we rate-limit client-exported flows to prevent NAT device serialization. takes effect as a QoS at the Redwood egress proxy.
[02:43] Maya: that sounds promising — is there any risk of inducing backpressure on our app?
[02:48] Lucas: minimal — the shaping is per-session and uses token buckets with a small burst budget. if you see head-of-line blocking we can reduce the burst size. but the initial tests show a 30% reduction in 99th tail spikes in our lab.
[03:03] Rafael: what about the kernel upgrade you proposed last week? we observed better throughput in bench but it introduced some ephemeral OOMs in staging.
[03:12] Priya: yeah the kernel/attn-optim patch gives better KV eviction behavior and reduced memory overhead, but on certain driver combos it can re-expose a race that we haven't pinned down.
[03:21] Anika: so is the rollback plan to go back to previous kernel? what's the risk of doing that mid-pilot?
[03:27] Priya: correct — the rollback is conservative: we can schedule a dry-run of the rollback on an isolated canary node, validate a smoke workload, then if green, gradually roll to the pilot nodes. risk is short downtime for that node during the rollback.
[03:40] Samir: how long is the canary smoke test? we need to fit within our maintenance window.
[03:44] Priya: we recommend a 2-hour burn with synthetic QPS and some KV miss patterns — that should surface the race if it's present.
[03:52] Maya: two hours is ok. can you provide the playbook so our ops team can run it too?
[03:58] Jordan: yea we'll send docs. action item for Priya to share runbench and Lucas to share exact traffic profiles.
[04:06] Rafael: audit and compliance question — any change here that would alter the audit logs or the KMS flow? last week we had a SOC 2 review and they asked about key rotations.
[04:16] Lucas: no change to KMS calls for the kernel work; keys remain in your HSM via the private deployment integration. we will not touch key material. audit logs remain intact, but we will add an extra trace field for the canary tests to make auditing simple.
[04:30] Anika: good. also our security team wanted to confirm Redwood supports SSO and RBAC for access to the console telemetry.
[04:36] Jordan: yes, SSO/SAML is available and we can scope a role-based view so Aurelia's engineers don't see cross-customer telemetry.
[04:44] Maya: quick data residency question: some of our traffic is EU-only. is the routing policy respecting region pins? we had a previous incident where cross-region routing accidentally bounced traffic to us-east.
[04:55] Priya: region pinning is enforced by policy — we will not route EU-bound flow to US nodes. the earlier incident was because of a misconfigured fallback policy which we've since flagged.
[05:06] Rafael: ok. about the KV warmup — you mentioned dedicated node approach?
[05:12] Lucas: yes, if you can tolerate a small reserved capacity we will provision a dedicated node for pre-warming the model KV-cache during off-peak hours. that reduces cold-start misses for short-turn calls.
[05:23] Samir: that will bump cost a bit, what's the expected uplift?
[05:27] Priya: rough estimate is 8–12% additional infra cost for a small dedicated warmup node, but you save about 20–30% on tail latency-derived user impact and retry cost.
[05:38] Anika: we need numbers to present to finance. can you provide a cost delta and projected SLA improvement?
[05:44] Jordan: yes, I'll add that to the pricing note.
[05:48] Maya: any experiments we should run this week?
[05:50] Priya: two things — 1) short smoke: enable egress shaping for 4 hours during peak and compare 95/99th; 2) run the 2-hour canary rollback dry-run as discussed.
[06:03] Rafael: we'll do the shaping test on Wednesday peak (2026-03-31), and the rollback dry-run we'll try Friday (2026-04-02) if that works.
[06:12] Lucas: FYI we'll need an ssh key and temporary SSO invite to the pilot console for the warmup node logs.
[06:18] Samir: send the exact ACLs and port list, we'll open on our side.
[06:22] Jordan: noted. Priya will share runbench and sample traces by Monday.
[06:28] Priya: one more note — we observed in the lab that quant fallback reduced 99th by ~40ms but increased some semantic drift on very long prompts; since your workload is short-turn, quant fallback is probably safe as a fallback path.
[06:42] Anika: ok we prefer no visible quality regression, so let's keep quant fallback as last resort.
[06:47] Jordan: wrapping up, recap of owners, next steps, and we'll set a check-in next Tuesday to review burn results.
[06:55] Maya: thanks everyone.
[07:00] Jordan: thanks, meeting adjourned.
